newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE WINS AFTER 'FALSE START'.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE WINS AFTER 'FALSE START'.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve justified his pre-season favourite status for the world championship on Sunday when he survived a 'false start' to win the Brazilian Grand Prix.
The Williams driver romped to victory by more than four seconds ahead of Austrian veteran Gerhard Berger, driving a Benetton.

But he owed his success to escaping another first lap, first corner exit, for the second successive race. Three weeks earlier in Australia, he had crashed out at the first corner -- this time when he was forced off, he recovered and rejoined close to the back and the race was red-flagged to a halt.
"That was lucky for me," he said later. "If that hadn't happened, I don't know where I would have been. I was glad to survive and then I was glad to win."

Villeneuve's fifth victory of his career and first of the season hoisted him alongside Briton David Coulthard of McLaren into the joint lead of the world drivers' championship with 10 points after two races.

Coulthard, victorious in Melbourne, finished 10th this time as Berger, Frenchman Olivier Panis in a Prost, Finn Mika Hakkinen in a McLaren, German Michael Schumacher in a Ferrari and Jean Alesi of France in a Benetton followed Villeneuve home.
Reigning champion Damon Hill, who was fifth at one stage in his Arrows, retired with four laps remaining.

The race began in sensational style with Villeneuve sliding off at the first corner following a near-collision with Schumacher. The Canadian rejoined unhurt as four other cars spun into chaos behind him.

In warm and humid conditions, the stewards brought out the red flag and stopped the race. It re-started 25 minutes later and this time Schumacher got away cleanly with a brilliant start, leaving Villeneuve in his wake as they hurtled down towards the Senna esses.
But Villeneuve was in a near-rage and he grabbed the lead with a dramatic charge at the end of the opening lap, passing the twice world champion's Ferrari as they braked at the end of the straight.
Villeneuve demonstrated his class by resisting a late charge by Berger to win with some ease and admitted afterwards he was relieved to escape after the first corner problems and then the red flag.

"I was very relieved because not only was I back in the race, but there were rocks and stones in the seat of my car and it was not very comfortable. That way, at least the mechanics were able to clean them out.
"It would have been pretty uncomfortable if the red flag hadn't come out...that would have changed the end result quite a bit.
"I was pushing hard at the end to resist Berger. My last set of tyres were pretty bad. The car was sliding around a lot. I had to work hard to hold it all the time."
